patch_description:
Crossover of the two (functionally identical) 2-parameter multi-shell CRZ ansatzes that both scored 0.61. Both prior seeds share the same backbone: a single global RY angle ("theta_ry") and a single global RZ angle ("theta_z") applied to every qubit, followed by CRZ entangling shells at ring-distances 1, 2 and 4 that reuse "theta_z". That design gets train=1.00/val=0.90/test=0.85 but has a sizeable generalization gap (0.15) and a comparatively low worst-group margin (0.33), suggesting the entangling layer is expressive along only the Z-generator direction and may be missing correlations that matter for the hardest validation group.

The crossover keeps the exact 2-distinct-parameter economy (still only theta_ry/theta_z, so parameter count and parameter-efficiency stay at their best-known value) but diversifies the *generator* of the entangling layer instead of just its range: the nearest-neighbor ring shell is duplicated with a CRY version that reuses "theta_ry" (no new parameter name), giving the circuit access to both a Z-type and a Y-type two-qubit coupling built from the same two global angles. This is a "generator interleaving" idea that mixes the seed's two independent single-qubit rotation axes into the entangling structure itself, which typically improves the richness of correlations captured near the readout without adding degrees of freedom to fit (and thus without hurting the small-training-set generalization behavior that parameter economy is being rewarded for). The distance-2 and distance-4 CRZ shells are kept unchanged since removing them was previously shown to hurt performance, and no final mixer layer is appended since that was previously shown to interact badly with a similarly-shelled 2-parameter circuit.

Net structural change vs. the current best (0.61) program: one additional CRY ring shell at distance 1, reusing "theta_ry", inserted right after the existing CRZ distance-1 shell. This keeps circuit depth/gate growth modest (8 extra gates per block, 24 extra across the 3 repeats) while giving the ansatz a genuinely 2-axis entangling structure, which should help align the state with the fixed two-qubit readout observable more robustly across validation subgroups (targeting the worst-group margin metric that dominates the score) while preserving the 2-parameter economy and fast convergence of the seed.
